key_insight: PI-GMDH adaptively builds the functional form of a physics-informed solution during training, rather than fixing the representation beforehand.
engineering_relevance: This can reduce model size and training cost while preserving high accuracy for fluid-flow surrogates and other PDE-constrained engineering problems.
method: Evaluate candidate functional terms using the first variation of the combined physics and observation objective.
Add useful terms progressively, then optimize coefficients with block-coordinate damped Gauss-Newton updates.
Demonstrate the approach on 2D time-dependent incompressible Navier-Stokes with tensor-product Chebyshev functions.
evidence_signal: On the Taylor-Green benchmark, the adaptive PI-GMDH variant reached validation and test losses of 5.299e-19 and 5.296e-19, with 204, 201, and 175 active functions for u, v, and p.
watch_item: The reported gains come from a controlled synthetic benchmark, so performance may not transfer directly to more complex or noisy real-world flows.
paper_title: Physics-Informed Method of Group Data Handling: Adaptive Construction of Functional Representations with an Application to the Navier-Stokes Equations
